metadata.note: The Frankfort and Cincinnati - 'The Whiskey Route' - a single 40.8-mile steam (later rail-motor-car) road Frankfort - Georgetown - Paris, Kentucky, that never reached Cincinnati. Built as the Kentucky Midland Railway (renamed from the Paris, Georgetown & Frankfort, 24 Feb 1888): Frankfort - Georgetown opened Jun 1889, Georgetown - Paris Feb 1890. Foreclosed 4 Jan 1897 and reorganised as the Frankfort and Cincinnati Railway (1897), Frankfort and Cincinnati Railroad from Jan 1927. Passenger service ended 31 Dec 1952. Three features: the Kentucky Midland era in its own new colour, split at Georgetown because the two halves opened in different years, and the F&C era in a second new colour over the same geometry joined (Rule 4 split by operator, at the 1897 reorganisation).
metadata.source: research/branches/frankfort_and_cincinnati_railroad.txt (2026-10-28): contemporary Kentucky newspapers on loc.gov (1889, 1897, 1898); lexhistory wiki 'Kentucky Midland Railway'; Wikipedia; American-Rails; KHS marker 2408; Official Guide Feb 1952.
metadata.freight_only_check: All freight years after 31 Dec 1952 trimmed, not drawn: Georgetown - Paris 1953-1967 (ICC abandonment 1967, rails up 1968), Georgetown - Elsinore 1953-1970, Frankfort - Elsinore and the distillery spurs 1953-1985 (trestle derailment closed the road 1985; last rails pulled 1987). The Stagg (Buffalo Trace) spur at Frankfort and the Stamping Ground / Buffalo Springs spur are freight-only and have no feature.
metadata.horsecar_check: None found, none trimmed: steam from opening in 1889.
metadata.ownership_split: Split at 1897 (by early March): Kentucky Midland Railway -> Frankfort and Cincinnati Railway after the 4 Jan 1897 foreclosure. The boundary year 1897 appears on both sides, following the repo convention for splits. Not splits: L&N stock control c.1901-1912 (no evidence the L&N ran the trains; the F&C kept its own officers, locomotives and timetable); the Jan 1927 reorganisation as the Frankfort and Cincinnati Railroad (same display company); the 1961 Pinsly purchase (after passengers ended).
metadata.colors: Both colours are new: neither 'Kentucky Midland' nor 'Frankfort and Cincinnati' appears anywhere else in data/ (grep, 2026-10-28), and #A67B19 / #A62C19 were checked programmatically against every colour in data/ (no exact match; chosen to maximise distance from existing colours).
not_yet_sourced: RENAME DATE CONFLICT: contemporary newspapers (Semi-Weekly Interior Journal 2 Mar 1897; Maysville Daily Public Ledger 15 Mar 1897; F&C Railway timetable ad in the Ledger 9 Apr 1898) put the reorganisation as the Frankfort and Cincinnati Railway in early 1897; Wikipedia, KHS marker 2408, abandonedrails and American-Rails say 1899. This layer follows the primary 1897 sources for the Rule 4 split; an ICC valuation report would settle it and was not consulted. If 1899 proves right for who ran the trains, the Kentucky Midland features should end 1899 and the F&C feature start 1899.

L&N control c.1901-1912: American-Rails says the L&N took the stock in 1901; Wikipedia mentions only the 1909 purchase annulled 22 Apr 1912. Whether L&N officers ran the trains in any of those years is not established; if they did, the F&C feature needs an L&N-coloured split.
Exact start date of Georgetown - Paris passenger trains in early 1890 ('placed in operation' Feb 1890 per lexhistory); the year is firm.
Last rail passenger trip probably 24 Dec 1952 (Cardinal axle failure), with a road substitute to 31 Dec 1952; whether a mixed train or the Cardinal carried the last passengers is not established.

headway_min (480 throughout) and avg_speed_kmh are estimates from scattered timetables (1892: two round trips plus partials; 1920: two round trips; 1951: apparently two round trips daily except Sunday).
Original charter date of the Paris, Georgetown & Frankfort Railway not established (irrelevant to drawn years).

segments.note: Kentucky Midland Railway's own trains, Frankfort - Elsinore (Forks of the Elkhorn) - Switzer - Stamping Ground - Georgetown. Built east from Frankfort by Mason, Gooch & Hoge from 1888; last spike near the Forks of the Elkhorn 1 Jun 1889; line opened 15 Jun 1889 (lexhistory citing Sulzer p.225). Semi-Weekly Interior Journal 14 Jun 1889: 'The Kentucky Midland has put on trains between Frankfort and Georgetown, which make the run in two hours'; Big Sandy News 13 Jun 1889: open for traffic. Steam from opening - no horse traction (Rule 5). Through running to Paris from Feb 1890 (see the Georgetown - Paris feature). Receivership Oct 1894 (receiver George B. Harper); foreclosure sale 4 Jan 1897. END 1897 IS AN ERA END, NOT A SERVICE END: reorganised as the Frankfort and Cincinnati Railway by early March 1897 (Semi-Weekly Interior Journal 2 Mar 1897; Maysville Daily Public Ledger 15 Mar 1897) and trains continued under that name - the F&C feature takes over in 1897. Secondary sources (Wikipedia, KHS marker 2408, American-Rails) date the rename 1899; see metadata.not_yet_sourced. headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE from the 1892 timetables (two through round trips plus two partial trips daily); no 1889-1891 frequency was read.
sources: Segment-level: start year from the June 1889 opening notices (Semi-Weekly Interior Journal 14 Jun 1889; Big Sandy News 13 Jun 1889) and lexhistory citing Sulzer; end year from the March 1897 rename notices. Headway is an estimate from the 1892 timetables via lexhistory.
Sulzer, Ghost Railroads of Kentucky (1967/1998) p.225 (via lexhistory; not consulted directly)

segments.note: Kentucky Midland's extension Georgetown - Newtown - Centerville - Elizabeth - Paris, completing the 40.8-mile Frankfort - Paris line. Last spike at Paris 2 Jan 1890; segment placed in operation Feb 1890 (lexhistory, citing Kentuckian-Citizen 4 Jan 1890 and Georgetown Times 8 Jan 1890; Wikipedia: Paris January 1890). Oct 1892 timetable: Train No. 1 Frankfort 6:00 a.m. - Paris 7:37 a.m. Fiscal year to 30 Jun 1892: 68,988 passengers on the road (Kentucky Railroad Commission via lexhistory). END 1897 IS AN ERA END (reorganisation as the Frankfort and Cincinnati Railway by early March 1897); service continued under the F&C feature. headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE from the 1892 timetables (two through round trips daily).
sources: Segment-level: start year from lexhistory citing the Kentuckian-Citizen (4 Jan 1890) and Georgetown Times (8 Jan 1890), agreeing with Wikipedia; end year from the March 1897 rename notices. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Frankfort and Cincinnati Railway (the 'Whiskey Route'), Frankfort - Elsinore - Switzer - Stamping Ground - Georgetown - Newtown - Centerville - Elizabeth - Paris, reorganised from the Kentucky Midland after the 4 Jan 1897 foreclosure sale. START 1897 follows the contemporary newspapers (Semi-Weekly Interior Journal 2 Mar 1897; Maysville Daily Public Ledger 15 Mar 1897: 'The Kentucky Midland has been renamed, and it is now the Frankfort and Cincinnati Railway'; F&C Railway timetable ad, Ledger 9 Apr 1898, Frankfort - Georgetown - Paris with Kentucky Central connections). Wikipedia, KHS marker 2408 and American-Rails say 1899 - conflict recorded in metadata.not_yet_sourced, not resolved. The L&N held the F&C's stock c.1901-1912 (purchase annulled 22 Apr 1912) but no evidence was found that it ran the trains, so no L&N split. Two round trips daily Frankfort - Paris by 1920 (American-Rails). Segment ends 1926 only because the company was sold at auction in Jan 1927 and reorganised as the Frankfort and Cincinnati Railroad - same display name, continuous service. headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE (two round trips a day, 1920).
sources: Segment-level: start year from the March 1897 rename notices and the April 1898 F&C timetable ad (conflicting with secondary sources' 1899); 1920 frequency from American-Rails. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Frankfort and Cincinnati Railroad (reorganised Jan 1927; not a Rule 4 split - same company name for display, same line, continuous service). From 1927 passengers rode two Brill Model 55 gasoline rail motor cars, painted red and nicknamed the 'Cardinal' (one survives at the Kentucky Railway Museum, NRHP 1998). Aug 1951 F&C table (Official Guide Feb 1952): Frankfort 7:09 - Georgetown 7:45 (mi 23) - Paris 8:22 (mi 41) and Frankfort 3:45 - Paris 5:12, a 'Mix' column, footnotes 'Daily, except Sunday' and 'Motor car' (the railroad's own rail motor car, not a bus). Passenger service ended 31 Dec 1952 (Wikipedia, American-Rails, KHS marker 2408 'Cardinal ran 1927-1952'); the Cardinal broke an axle 24 Dec 1952 and the superintendent drove the last week's passengers by car, so the last rail trip was c.24 Dec 1952 - year unaffected. Freight continued (Georgetown - Paris abandoned 1967, Georgetown - Elsinore 1970, Frankfort end closed 1985, rails up 1987); none of those years is drawn (Rule 1). headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE (apparently two round trips daily except Sunday in 1951).
sources: Segment-level: end year from Wikipedia, American-Rails, the KHS marker and the Model 55 Rail Car article (NRHP nomination), with the Aug 1951 timetable in the Feb 1952 Official Guide confirming service near the end; 1927 start of this era from the Jan 1927 reorganisation and the Cardinal's 1927 introduction. Headway is an estimate.
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt), Frankfort & Cincinnati Railroad Co. table dated Aug 1951
